requirements.feishuCliAuth: Do not hardcode a fixed Feishu CLI setup path in WebUI; run structured tool diagnostics and let the agent/tool choose the official lark-cli flow.
requirements.externalConnections: All external connections expose an agent-discovery contract; WebUI displays and forwards declared actions but does not own vendor setup flow logic.
requirements.tongxinCli: Tongxin/Xin Assistant can be auto-configured from trusted local script or configured remote account login followed by SHA256-verified bootstrap; disclosed data remains read-only and permission-visible only; bad local script copies that pass schema but fail the data layer are rejected.
requirements.antiRegression: Tests and prompt rules block fallback to default domain=base, raw auth-login default-domain routing, Feishu-only Web action checks, legacy CLI-auth labeling, and config_init as the catalog default.

antiRegressionSearches: name == feishu agent auth action special-case
notes: Feishu status nextAction now points to feishu_cli agent_auth, not auth_login domain=base.
Raw lark auth login without explicit scope/domain is autorouted to feishu_cli agent_auth; explicit official scope/domain flags are preserved without inventing defaults.
Web External Connections call feishu_cli agent_auth without passing saved app fields, so the visible CLI URL path is not bypassed by static app-field setup.
Web-facing Feishu setup copy now says Agent setup instead of implying Web owns a fixed CLI setup flow.
Tongxin default capability install now proxies to auto_configure when no explicit local script path is supplied.
Explicit remote URL/inline ticket bootstrap remains outside default read-only permission; config-driven auth/bootstrap is allowed.

Tongxin configure/auto_configure/bootstrap/run now use a schema plus read-only project-list data-layer health probe; scripts that fail with models.DATABASE are reported as dependency_failed and are not persisted.
Tongxin bootstrap probes the candidate script in the final target directory, restores the previous script on health failure, and only persists a path after the final target-dir probe passes.
Nash cross-review returned PASS after the target-dir bootstrap health blocker was fixed.
